record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Unbounded extremal solutions in high dimension
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded smooth convex subset of R^N with N≥10, and consider -Δu=λe^u in Ω, u>0 in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω. Let u* be the extremal weak solution obtained as λ increases to the critical parameter λ*. Is u* unbounded? If some convex domains have bounded u* for f(u)=e^u, can one find another smooth increasing convex superlinear nonlinearity f, possibly depending on Ω and satisfying f(0)>0 and f(t)/t→∞, for which the corresponding extremal solution u* is not in L∞(Ω)?

evidence.quote: Consider the nonlinear elliptic equation (6.1) -Δu = λf(u) in Ω ⊂ RN, u > 0 in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, where Ω is a smooth bounded domain in RN, λ > 0 is a constant, and f : [0, +∞) → (0, +∞) is a smooth function satisfying (6.2) f(0) > 0, f is increasing and convex, and (6.3) limt→∞ f(t)/t = +∞.

Open Problem 6.1 ([BrVa], [Br6]). Assume Ω is a bounded smooth convex set in RN, N ≥ 10. Let f(u) = eu. Is u∗ unbounded? If the answer is negative for some domains Ω, can one find other functions f satisfying (6.2)-(6.3) (possibly depending on Ω) such that u∗ ∈/ L∞(Ω)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded smooth convex domain with $N \ge 10$. For a smooth function $f:[0,\infty) \to (0,\infty)$ satisfying $f(0)>0$, $f$ increasing and convex, and $\lim_{t\to\infty} f(t)/t = +\infty$, consider the family of problems
$$-\Delta u = \lambda f(u) \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u > 0 \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
for $\lambda > 0$. It is known that there exists a critical parameter $\lambda^* = \lambda^*(\Omega,f) \in (0,\infty)$ such that for every $\lambda \in (0,\lambda^*)$ the problem admits a minimal classical solution $u_\lambda$, the family $\{u_\lambda\}$ is increasing in $\lambda$, and the pointwise limit
$$u^*(x) := \lim_{\lambda \nearrow \lambda^*} u_\lambda(x)$$
defines the so-called extremal weak solution of the problem at $\lambda = \lambda^*$.

(a) Taking $f(u) = e^u$, is the extremal solution $u^*$ necessarily unbounded (i.e. $u^* \notin L^\infty(\Omega)$) for every bounded smooth convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ with $N \ge 10$?

(b) If there exist bounded smooth convex domains $\Omega$ for which the extremal solution corresponding to $f(u) = e^u$ is bounded, does there always exist some smooth function $f$ (possibly depending on $\Omega$) satisfying the conditions $f(0)>0$, $f$ increasing and convex, and $f(t)/t \to \infty$ as $t \to \infty$, such that the corresponding extremal solution $u^*$ is not in $L^\infty(\Omega)$?
artifact.category_tag: Extremal solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
artifact.status_search_result: For general (not necessarily exponential) nonlinearities, the regularity of extremal solutions in dimensions $N\le 9$ was settled by Cabré–Figalli–Ros-Oton–Serra, and constructions show that for $N\ge 10$ there exist domains and nonlinearities $f$ producing singular extremal solutions, addressing part (b) affirmatively in a strong sense. However, for the specific case $f(u)=e^u$ on general bounded smooth convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $N\ge 10$, the question of whether $u^*$ must be unbounded remains open in general (it is known only on balls via Joseph–Lundgren).

status_evidence.title: Boundedness of Stable Solutions to Semilinear Elliptic Equations: A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Joseph and Lundgren proved that u* is unbounded for f(u)=e^u when N≥10; regularity in N≤9 for general f was a longstanding open problem.
status_evidence.claim: For the exponential nonlinearity the result is classical on radial/ball domains; the convex general domain case in N≥10 has not been fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Some of my favorite open problems — H. Brezis
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 6.1 asks whether u* is unbounded for f=e^u on convex Ω in R^N, N≥10.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as open.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of stable solutions up to dimension 9 (Cabré–Figalli–Ros-Oton–Serra)
status_evidence.snippet: Extremal solutions are bounded for all f and all smooth domains in dimensions N≤9; counterexamples exist for N≥10 with suitable f.
status_evidence.claim: Part (b) of the problem is essentially resolved by counterexamples in high dimensions for some nonlinearity f.
